intro: On the shore of Lake Bafa, among the boulders of the Beşparmak range, lies Heracleia under Latmus, an ancient city in Muğla province from the 4th century BC. Its Hellenistic walls run six kilometres around the slope.
history: The city was built among the granite boulders of the Beşparmak range, on the shore of what was then a sea gulf. Then the Meander did its slow work: its silt closed the gulf, the sea became Lake Bafa, and the harbour town was left inland. Around the slope, its Hellenistic walls run for six kilometres.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Hellenistic walls and the temple of Athena, then the agora and the rock tombs.
facts: Did you know? The rock paintings in the Latmos hills go back to the sixth millennium BC, and they are the oldest pictorial narratives known in western Anatolia. And Lake Bafa was once a sea gulf: silt from the Meander closed it and left the harbour town inland.
outro: This brings our tour of Heracleia under Latmus to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Among these boulders, take a quiet moment before you go. Enjoy your visit.
